title: Florida JEAC Opinion 2026-02
subject: A judicial candidate may use on their campaign website and on social media a photograph depicting the candidate being sworn in as a member of the Florida Bar by a retired judge who is not eligible for recall to active judicial service. 2B; JEAC Ops. 2001-04, 2008-10, 2008-11, 2010-18, 2016-09.
text:
ISSUE
Whether a judicial candidate may use on their campaign website and on social media a photograph depicting the candidate being sworn in as a member of the Florida Bar by a retired judge.
aNSWER: Yes.

FACTS
The inquiring candidate has received an unsolicited endorsement from a retired judge. The candidate would like to use a photograph of the retired judge swearing the candidate in as a member of the Florida Bar. The retired judge is now a practicing attorney who is not subject to recall to active judicial service and is, therefore, no longer subject to the Florida Code of Judicial Conduct. See Fla. Code Jud. Conduct, Application, B(2).

DISCUSSION
We have previously opined that judicial candidates “should avoid use of photographs depicting other judges, both in campaign literature and on any web site.” Fla. JEAC Op. 08 - 11. This is so even if “the photograph depicts an historical event and was not staged for campaign purposes.” Fla. JEAC Op. 10-18.
In the present inquiry, however, the judge in robes is retired and not subject to recall to active service. Because the retired judge is not subject to the Code, the retired judge is free to endorse any candidate, judicial or political, without fear of violating Canon 2B (“A judge shall not lend the prestige of judicial office to advance the private interests of the judge or others”). The inquiring candidate, in turn, is free to accept the endorsement because it is not from a judge or a partisan endorsement from an elected official who is running for election. See Opinion 16-09 (judicial candidate may accept and advertise endorsement from county commissioner who plans to run for re-election in future election cycle if endorsement is from individual – and not political party that person represents – and the partisan aspect of that official’s position is not mentioned).
Although the thought of a picture of the retired judge in judicial robes may at first blush appear improper, we conclude it is not. First, the picture is not misleading because the retired judge is pictured wearing a judicial robe at a time the retired judge was in fact a judge; the retired judge is in fact endorsing the candidate; and the retired judge did in fact swear the candidate into the Florida Bar. See Fla. JEAC Op. 08- 11 (“Judge’s campaign signs may include pictures of the Judge wearing the judicial robe. Because the inquirer is an incumbent judge seeking re-election the answer is yes. Under these circumstances, there is no chance that such advertisement will mislead the voting public about the Judge’s professional history.”).
Second, we have previously opined that a candidate can publicize an endorsement from a retired judge – while identifying the endorser as a former judge. See Fla. JEAC Op. 01-04 (retired judge can participate in son’s judicial campaign and make a financial contribution); Fla. JEAC Op. 08- 10 (even a judicial candidate running for office can “use the term ‘former judge’ or ‘retired judge’ in campaign literature, media releases, printed ads, or other media venues”).

REFERENCES
Fla. Code Jud. Conduct, Canon 2B, Application.
Fla. JEAC Ops. 2001-04, 2008-10, 2008-11, 2010-18, 2016-09

SUBJECT
A judicial candidate may use on their campaign website and on social media a photograph depicting the candidate being sworn in as a member of the Florida Bar by a retired judge who is not eligible for recall to active judicial service. 2B; JEAC Ops. 2001-04, 2008-10, 2008-11, 2010-18, 2016-09.
